payload.title: Director of People Operations
payload.description:
A family-owned construction company, headquartered in Wichita, needs someone to lead its people team. Most of the foundation got built in the last 18 months, and the next director gets to build what’s still missing, starting with a performance management system that managers will use. Over time, the role grows into ownership of the company’s people strategy.

About 400 team members work across several offices in Kansas. The business has added roughly 100 people in five years and expects the same pace over the next five. There’s no outside capital and no exit timeline. The owners run it, and the leaders are independent people who want to do the right thing and would rather be shown where the line is than handed a rulebook.

About half of those team members are in the field, on projects led by people who are almost never at a desk. You go to them: most weeks that’s the Wichita office, and one or two days a month it’s a job site or regional office. You lead a team of five from day one. You report to the VP of People Operations through the handoff. You run the team and the day-to-day from the start; she steps back once the transition is done, and you lead the people function and own the company’s people strategy.

payload.title: Director of Sales
payload.description:
A Hampton Roads contractor with decades of Navy work and shops that can take on far more than they carry today is hiring the person who will give its sales function structure. There is a rep, three estimators and a customer base, but no pipeline discipline and no playbook. The Director of Sales writes both, holds one of the five seats on the leadership team, and has the authority to hire. Year one is a selling year: take the long-cycle customer relationships off the President’s plate, get in front of the people at the largest accounts who decide where multi-year work goes, and land the contracts that make growth predictable.

For nearly 40 years the company ran on reputation. The Naval Industrial Base kept sending work, industrial customers who called once kept calling, and sales ran on relationships rather than a system. It is an industrial services contractor serving shipbuilding, defense and manufacturing customers, with revenue approaching eight figures. Most of that is Department of Defense work, often subcontracted through the large shipbuilders that hold the Navy contracts; the rest is direct business with industrial and commercial customers, where the most growth is available. A private holding company with no plans to sell owns the business, and the President has spent two years adding structure.

payload.title: Sr. Data Engineer with modern architecture & agentic AI experience
payload.description:
The Talent Mine is partnering with a major US steel manufacturer to hire a Senior Data Engineer for an immediate, on-site FTE role in either Charlotte, NC or Irvine, TX. This client is the nation's #1 recycler of any product, a company with unmatched job security and stable growth!

 

***NOTE: Our clients are NOT able to consider candidates with H1B/OPT-EAD/C2C work authorization status or visa sponsorship requirements.***

 

The Senior Data Engineer plays a critical role by designing, building, and optimizing scalable data platforms and intelligent data workflows to advance the client’s data and automation initiatives. This role enables high-quality, trusted data products while leveraging agentic automation frameworks and modern lake house architectures to drive efficiency and innovation.

This position combines deep technical expertise in data engineering with emerging capabilities in automated, self-orchestrating data systems. The Senior Data Engineer works closely with cross-functional teams to deliver data-driven solutions, automate complex data processes, and support real-time decision-making across the enterprise.
